chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adamy, who said: Uthman ibn Isa narrated to me, from Khalid ibn Najih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

They discussed bad omen in his presence, so he said: Bad omen is in three things: in the woman, the riding animal, and the house. As for the bad omen of the woman, it is the abundance of her dowry and the disobedience of her husband; as for the animal, it is its bad character and withholding its back (for riding); and as for the house, it is its narrow yard, its bad neighbors, and the abundance of its defects.
ai.seo_question: What are the three things that carry a bad omen according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) contextualizes 'shoom' (ill-omen) not as superstition but as a reflection of practical social and domestic realities, linking material conditions to spiritual well-being. He identifies excessive dowry and marital discord in women, stubbornness in animals, and poor living conditions in dwellings as key factors that invite misfortune, emphasizing the interplay between environment and character. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on aligning one’s external circumstances with internal virtues to maintain harmony and divine favor.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-53 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Sahl ibn Zyad al-Adamy, on the authority of Uthman ibn Isa, on the authority of Khalid ibn Najih, “The issue of bad omen was brought up in the presence of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB).

The Imam (MGB) said, ‘There is a bad omen in three things: women, riding animals and houses. The thing with bad omen in women is the greatness of the nuptial gift and the displeasure of her husband; the thing with bad omen in riding an animal is in its not being tamed and not giving a ride; and the thing with bad omen in a house is in its small yard, bad neighbors and its many shortcomings.”
